name: Beijing Lu Xun Museum (Lu Xun's home at Xisantiao)
name_zh: 北京鲁迅博物馆（西三条鲁迅故居）
note: 鲁迅 1924 到 1926 年住在阜成门内西三条这座小四合院，《野草》《彷徨》里的许多篇就写在后院一间被他叫作“老虎尾巴”的小屋里，《秋夜》开头那两株枣树就长在院墙外。故居保持着他离开时的样子，旁边是收藏手稿和遗物的鲁迅博物馆
note_en: Lu Xun lived in this small courtyard house at Xisantiao from 1924 to 1926 and wrote much of Wild Grass and Wandering in the cramped back room he called the Tiger's Tail; the two jujube trees that open 'Autumn Night' stood just beyond the wall. The house is kept as he left it, beside a museum of his manuscripts and belongings

name: Lao She Memorial Hall (the Red Persimmon Courtyard)
note: 写出《骆驼祥子》和《茶馆》的老舍是地道的北京人，1950 年回国后一直住在灯市口这座小四合院，《茶馆》就是在这里写成的。他和夫人在院里种了两棵柿子树，秋天满树红柿，朋友们叫它“丹柿小院”。书房和客厅照原样陈列，院子里的柿子树还在
note_en: Lao She, author of Rickshaw Boy and Teahouse, was a Beijinger through and through. After returning to China in 1950 he lived in this little courtyard house near Dengshikou until his death in 1966, and wrote Teahouse here. He and his wife planted two persimmon trees, which turn the yard red each autumn, so friends called it the Red Persimmon Courtyard. His study and sitting room are kept as they were, and the trees are still there

name: Lugou Bridge (Marco Polo Bridge)
note: 马可·波罗 13 世纪末在游记里写到大都城外十英里的一座大石桥，说它“美得世上少有可比”，还细细描写了桥栏上的石狮。西方人从此把卢沟桥叫作“马可·波罗桥”。这座金代石桥今天仍横跨永定河，栏杆上的石狮据说有五百多只，1937 年七七事变也发生在这里
note_en: Marco Polo describes a great stone bridge ten miles outside Kublai Khan's capital, 'so fine indeed that it has very few equals', down to the marble lions on its parapets, and the West has called Lugou Bridge the Marco Polo Bridge ever since. The twelfth-century bridge still spans the Yongding River with its hundreds of carved lions, and the Marco Polo Bridge Incident of 1937 that began the war with Japan happened here

name: Cao Yu's former residence, Tianjin
note: 写《雷雨》的剧作家曹禺在天津长大，这座意大利风格小楼是他少年时的家。他在南开中学开始演话剧，二十三岁写出《雷雨》，剧中那个大家庭里压抑的气氛，被认为有他童年的影子。小楼今天是曹禺纪念馆，就在原意租界的民主道上
note_en: Cao Yu, author of the play Thunderstorm, grew up in Tianjin, and this Italianate house was his boyhood home. He began acting in plays at Nankai Middle School and wrote Thunderstorm at twenty-three; the stifling family household of the play is often said to draw on his own childhood. The house, on Minzhu Road in the old Italian Concession, is now a museum to him
coord_checked: File:民主道25号曹禺旧居.jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:民主道25号曹禺旧居.jpg

name: Baiyangdian Lake
note: 孙犁的小说《荷花淀》写的就是这片华北最大的淡水湖：抗战时期，水生嫂和村里的妇女摇着小船进荷花淀找参加了游击队的丈夫，在一望无际的荷叶里遇上了日本人的汽船。白洋淀今天仍是芦苇荡、荷塘和水村，夏天坐船进淀，荷花开得正盛
note_en: Sun Li's story 'Lotus Creek' is set on Baiyangdian, the largest freshwater lake in northern China. During the war with Japan, Shuisheng's wife and the other village women row out into the lotus marshes to look for their husbands, who have joined the guerrillas, and run into a Japanese motor launch among the endless lotus leaves. The lake is still a maze of reed beds, lotus ponds and water villages, and in summer you can take a boat out when the lotuses are in bloom

name: Pujiu Temple, Yongji
note: 《西厢记》的故事就发生在这座寺里：书生张生借住普救寺，在西厢遇见暂居寺中的崔莺莺，靠丫鬟红娘牵线，终于有情人成了眷属。“愿天下有情人都成了眷属”这句话就出自这部戏。今天寺里有梨花院、西厢房和一座据说能传出蛙鸣回声的“莺莺塔”
note_en: The Romance of the Western Chamber is set in this temple: the young scholar Zhang lodges here, meets Cui Yingying in the western wing where her family is staying, and with the help of her maid Hongniang the two lovers are finally united; the line 'may all lovers under heaven be united' comes from the play. Today you can see the Pear Blossom Courtyard, the western wing and the Yingying Pagoda, whose brickwork is said to echo like a croaking frog

name: Zhaojun Tomb (the Green Mound), Hohhot
name_zh: 呼和浩特 · 昭君墓（青冢）
note: 汉代宫女王昭君远嫁匈奴单于，成了历代诗人反复吟咏的人物；杜甫在《咏怀古迹》里写她“一去紫台连朔漠，独留青冢向黄昏”，青冢说的就是这座墓。传说塞外草木秋天枯黄，唯独这座墓上的草四季常青。今天墓前有昭君和单于并辔而行的铜像和一座博物馆
note_en: Wang Zhaojun, a palace lady of the Han dynasty sent to marry the Xiongnu khan, became one of the great subjects of Chinese poetry; Du Fu writes of her 'leaving the purple palace for the northern desert, and only the Green Mound left, facing the dusk', and the Green Mound is this tomb. Legend says that when the grass beyond the Wall turned brown in autumn, the grass on her grave stayed green. A bronze of Zhaojun and the khan riding side by side stands before the tomb, with a museum beside it

name: Ergun, by the Argun River
note: 迟子建的《额尔古纳河右岸》写的是额尔古纳河右岸大兴安岭森林里，一支养驯鹿的鄂温克人近百年的命运，由部落最后一位酋长的妻子在一天之内讲完，获得了茅盾文学奖。额尔古纳市是走进这片林区和湿地的门户，城外就是亚洲最大的湿地之一，往北是中俄界河
note_en: Chi Zijian's The Last Quarter of the Moon tells a century in the life of a clan of reindeer-herding Evenki in the forests of the Greater Khingan along the right bank of the Argun River, narrated over a single day by the wife of their last chieftain; it won the Mao Dun Literature Prize. The town of Ergun is the gateway to these forests and wetlands, with one of Asia's largest wetlands just outside town and the river that forms the border with Russia to the north

name: Fushun War Criminals Management Centre
note: 末代皇帝溥仪在自传《我的前半生》里写了他在这里的十年：1950 年他被苏联移交回国，关进抚顺战犯管理所，第一次学着自己穿衣、洗衣、糊纸盒，直到 1959 年特赦。这里后来成了陈列馆，监舍、溥仪住过的房间和当年的劳动场景都保留着
note_en: In his autobiography From Emperor to Citizen, the last emperor Puyi describes his ten years here. Handed back to China by the Soviet Union in 1950, he was held at the Fushun War Criminals Management Centre, where for the first time in his life he learned to dress himself, wash his own clothes and glue paper boxes, until his pardon in 1959. It is now a museum, with the cells, Puyi's own room and the workshops preserved
coord_checked: Fushun War Criminals Management Center (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Fushun_War_Criminals_Management_Center

name: Museum of the Imperial Palace of Manchukuo, Changchun
name_zh: 长春 · 伪满皇宫博物院
note: 1932 年日本扶植溥仪做“满洲国”的傀儡元首，他在这片由盐务署改成的宫苑里住了十三年，《我的前半生》里写了他在这里的屈辱和恐惧，直到 1945 年仓皇出逃。宫殿保留着溥仪的书房、寝宫和他打网球的球场，还有讲述日本侵华历史的展览
note_en: In 1932 Japan installed Puyi as the puppet ruler of Manchukuo, and for thirteen years he lived in this palace compound, converted from a salt tax office; From Emperor to Citizen recalls his humiliation and fear here, until he fled in 1945. You can see his study, his bedrooms and the tennis court he played on, alongside exhibitions on the Japanese occupation
coord_checked: Museum of the Imperial Palace of the Manchu State (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Museum_of_the_Imperial_Palace_of_the_Manchu_State

name: Xiao Hong's former residence, Hulan
note: 萧红 1911 年生在哈尔滨呼兰区这座宅院里，《呼兰河传》写的就是这座小城和这个家：她最爱跟着祖父待在后花园，蝴蝶、蚂蚱、黄瓜架，“花开了，就像花睡醒了似的”。故居有正房、厢房和那座后花园，院里立着萧红的雕像
note_en: Xiao Hong was born in 1911 in this house in Hulan, north of Harbin, and Tales of Hulan River is the story of this small town and this home. Her happiest hours were spent with her grandfather in the back garden among the butterflies, grasshoppers and cucumber vines, where 'the flowers bloomed as if they had just woken up'. You can visit the main house, the side rooms and the back garden, where a statue of her now stands
coord_checked: File:Harbin Scenes 哈爾濱景色 (1791501745).jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Harbin_Scenes_哈爾濱景色_(1791501745).jpg

name: Tomb of Lu Xun, Luxun Park, Shanghai
name_zh: 上海 · 鲁迅墓（鲁迅公园）
note: 鲁迅生命的最后十年住在上海虹口，写下大量杂文，1936 年在大陆新村的寓所去世，出殡那天上万人自发送行。1956 年他的墓迁到虹口公园，公园后来改名鲁迅公园。墓前有他的坐像，墓碑上是毛泽东手书的“鲁迅先生之墓”，旁边就是上海鲁迅纪念馆
note_en: Lu Xun spent the last ten years of his life in Hongkou, Shanghai, writing hundreds of essays, and died at his flat in the Dalu Xincun lane in 1936; tens of thousands followed his funeral, his coffin draped in a banner reading 'Soul of the Nation'. In 1956 his grave was moved to Hongkou Park, since renamed Luxun Park. A seated statue of him faces the tomb, and the Shanghai Lu Xun Museum is next door

name: Changde Apartments (Eddington House), Shanghai
name_zh: 上海 · 常德公寓（爱丁顿公寓）
note: 张爱玲 1942 年从香港回到上海，和姑姑住在这座公寓的六楼，《倾城之恋》《金锁记》都在这里写成，她在散文里写过在阳台上听电车的声音入睡。两年间她从一个年轻作者成了上海最红的作家。这座装饰艺术风格的公寓楼至今有人居住，门口挂着张爱玲旧居的牌子
note_en: Eileen Chang came back to Shanghai from Hong Kong in 1942 and lived with her aunt on the sixth floor of this building, where she wrote Love in a Fallen City and The Golden Cangue; her essays recall falling asleep to the sound of the trams below the balcony. In two years she went from unknown to the most talked-about writer in the city. The Art Deco block is still lived in, with a plaque at the door marking her home
coord_checked: File:常德公寓·爱林登公寓·上海.jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:常德公寓·爱林登公寓·上海.jpg

name: Hanshan Temple, Suzhou
note: 张继一首《枫桥夜泊》让城外这座小寺成了天下最有名的寺院之一：“姑苏城外寒山寺，夜半钟声到客船”。诗里的枫桥就在寺旁运河上，还在。每年除夕，许多人专程来寺里听新年钟声，日本游客尤其多，因为这首诗在日本也家喻户晓
note_en: One short poem, Zhang Ji's 'A Night Mooring by Maple Bridge', made this little temple outside Suzhou one of the most famous in China: 'Outside the walls of Gusu, Hanshan Temple; its midnight bell reaches the traveller's boat'. The Maple Bridge of the poem still crosses the canal beside it. Every New Year's Eve crowds come to hear the temple bell ring in the year, many of them from Japan, where the poem is just as well known

name: Canglang Pavilion, Suzhou
note: 沈复在《浮生六记》开篇就说自己生在“苏州沧浪亭畔”，新婚那年中秋，他和妻子芸第一次走进隔壁的沧浪亭，在假山顶的亭子里铺毯席地而坐，烹茶看月。这是苏州现存最古老的园林，北宋苏舜钦所建，园外一湾清水，亭子仍在土山顶上
note_en: Shen Fu opens Six Records of a Floating Life by saying he was born 'beside the Canglang Pavilion in Suzhou', and in the first autumn of his marriage he and his wife Yun slip into the garden next door one Mid-Autumn night, spread a rug in the pavilion on the hilltop, brew tea and watch the moon rise. It is the oldest surviving garden in Suzhou, laid out in the eleventh century, with water along its outer wall and the pavilion still on its little hill

name: Qinhuai River by the Confucius Temple, Nanjing
name_zh: 南京 · 秦淮河（夫子庙）
note: 六朝古都的秦淮河是中国诗文里最有名的一段河：杜牧夜泊秦淮，听见隔江歌女还唱着亡国之曲《后庭花》，写下“商女不知亡国恨”；《桃花扇》的李香君、朱自清的《桨声灯影里的秦淮河》也都在这里。今天夫子庙一带夜里画舫灯火通明，正是诗里的景象
note_en: The Qinhuai, flowing through the old capital of six dynasties, is the most storied stretch of river in Chinese writing: Du Mu moors here one night and hears a singing girl across the water still singing a song of a fallen court, 'not knowing the grief of a lost kingdom'. The Peach Blossom Fan and Zhu Ziqing's essay on its lantern-lit waters are set here too. At night by the Confucius Temple the painted boats are still lit up just as in the poem
coord_checked: File:Confucius Temple, Qinhuai, Nanjing, Jiangsu, China, 210001 - panoramio (4).jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Confucius_Temple,_Qinhuai,_Nanjing,_Jiangsu,_China,_210001_-_panoramio_(4).jpg

name: Mount Huaguo, Lianyungang
prototype_of: 《西游记》里孙悟空的老家花果山，一般认为就以连云港这座海边的云台山为原型：吴承恩写花果山在东海之滨，山上有仙石，石猴从里面蹦出来，还有瀑布后面的水帘洞。这座山明清时还是海中的岛，后来海岸东移才连上陆地，今天山上有水帘洞、娘娘殿和成群的猴子
prototype_of_en: The Mount of Flowers and Fruit, home of the Monkey King in Journey to the West, is generally taken to be modelled on this seaside mountain at Lianyungang: Wu Cheng'en sets it beside the eastern sea, with the magic stone the stone monkey bursts from and the Water Curtain Cave behind a waterfall. In Ming times the mountain was still an island before the coast moved east, and today you can visit a Water Curtain Cave and a temple, with plenty of monkeys about

name: Pearl S. Buck's former residence, Nanjing University
name_zh: 南京大学 · 赛珍珠故居
note: 赛珍珠在中国长大，1919 到 1934 年住在金陵大学校园里这座小楼，在阁楼上写出了讲安徽农民王龙一家命运的《大地》，1938 年凭着她写中国的作品成为第一位获得诺贝尔文学奖的美国女作家。小楼在今天的南京大学北园，是一座纪念馆
note_en: Pearl S. Buck grew up in China and from 1919 to 1934 lived in this house on the campus of the University of Nanking, where in an attic room she wrote The Good Earth, the story of the farmer Wang Lung and his family. In 1938 her writing about China made her the first American woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature. The house, on the north campus of today's Nanjing University, is a small museum
coord_checked: Former Residence of Pearl S. Buck in Nanjing (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Former_Residence_of_Pearl_S._Buck_in_Nanjing

name: Mid-Lake Pavilion, West Lake, Hangzhou
note: 明末张岱的《湖心亭看雪》只有一百多字，却是写西湖最有名的文字之一：大雪三日之后的夜里，他独自撑一叶小舟去湖心亭，天、云、山、水上下一白，湖上只剩“长堤一痕，湖心亭一点”。湖心亭在西湖正中的小岛上，今天坐游船可以登岛
note_en: Zhang Dai's 'Viewing the Snow from the Mid-Lake Pavilion' is barely a paragraph long, yet it is one of the best-loved pieces ever written on West Lake: after three days of snow he rows out alone at night to the pavilion, and sky, cloud, hills and water are one white, with nothing on the lake but 'a trace of the long causeway, a dot of the pavilion'. The pavilion stands on a small island in the middle of the lake, and tour boats stop there

name: Lu Xun Native Place, Shaoxing
note: 鲁迅 1881 年生在绍兴城里这条街上的周家新台门，童年的百草园和三味书屋都在这里，小说《故乡》里那个回乡卖掉老屋的“我”，写的就是他 1919 年回绍兴搬家的经历。今天故居、百草园、三味书屋和他外婆家所在的鲁镇风情都连成一片街区
note_en: Lu Xun was born in 1881 in the Zhou family mansion on this street in Shaoxing, and the Hundred Plant Garden and the Three Flavours Study of his childhood essays are here too. In the story 'My Old Home' the narrator comes back to sell the family house, as Lu Xun himself did in 1919. His house, the garden, the old school room and the streets around them are now one historic quarter
coord_checked: File:鲁迅故居 Luxun native place - panoramio.jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:鲁迅故居_Luxun_native_place_-_panoramio.jpg

name: Xianheng Tavern, Shaoxing
note: 鲁迅的《孔乙己》开篇就写“鲁镇的酒店”和咸亨酒店：曲尺形的大柜台，短衣帮站着喝酒，唯一穿长衫而站着喝酒的是孔乙己，一碟茴香豆，“多乎哉？不多也”。咸亨酒店是鲁迅的堂叔真开过的店，今天照小说的样子重开，门口立着孔乙己像，柜台上照样卖黄酒和茴香豆
note_en: Lu Xun's story 'Kong Yiji' opens in the tavern of Lu Town, the Xianheng: a big L-shaped counter, working men drinking standing up, and Kong Yiji, the only man in a scholar's long gown who drinks standing, with his saucer of aniseed beans. A relative of Lu Xun really ran a Xianheng Tavern; it has been reopened in the image of the story, with a statue of Kong Yiji at the door and yellow wine and aniseed beans still on the counter
coord_checked: File:咸亨酒店 Xian Heng Restaurant - panoramio.jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:咸亨酒店_Xian_Heng_Restaurant_-_panoramio.jpg

name: Tiandu Peak, Huangshan
note: 明代旅行家徐霞客两游黄山，第二次不顾僧人劝阻，攀上当时“无路”的天都峰顶，看见“万峰无不下伏”，云雾一会儿把群峰吞成银海、一会儿又吐出来。他的游记是中国最有名的山水文字之一。天都峰今天是黄山最险的一条登山路，要走过窄窄的“鲫鱼背”
note_en: The Ming traveller Xu Xiake climbed Huangshan twice, and the second time, ignoring the monks who told him there was no way up, he scrambled to the top of Tiandu Peak, where 'ten thousand peaks all bowed below' as the mist swallowed them into a silver sea and gave them back again. His diaries are among the most famous travel writing in Chinese. The route up Tiandu is still the steepest on Huangshan, over the knife-edge called the Carp's Back
coord_checked: File:天都峰全景 - Panorama of the Celestial Capital Peak - 2010.05 - panoramio.jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:天都峰全景_-_Panorama_of_the_Celestial_Capital_Peak_-_2010.05_-_panoramio.jpg

name: Old Drunkard's Pavilion, Chuzhou
note: 欧阳修贬官滁州时常带着客人到琅琊山的这座亭子里喝酒，自号“醉翁”，写下“醉翁之意不在酒，在乎山水之间也”。《醉翁亭记》开头“环滁皆山也”几个字，几乎每个中国学生都背过。亭子在琅琊山半山腰的酿泉边，旁边还有苏轼手书的碑
note_en: Exiled to Chuzhou, Ouyang Xiu often brought guests to drink at this pavilion on Langya Mountain and called himself the Old Drunkard, writing that 'the old drunkard's heart is not in the wine but in the hills and streams'. The opening words of his essay, 'Chuzhou is ringed by hills', are known by heart by almost every Chinese schoolchild. The pavilion stands halfway up the mountain beside the Brewing Spring, with a stele of the essay in Su Shi's hand nearby

name: Former Residence of Lin Juemin, Fuzhou
name_zh: 福州 · 林觉民故居（冰心故居）
note: 1911 年广州起义前夜，二十四岁的林觉民写下《与妻书》，信里回忆“后街之屋”的小厅旁一间屋就是他和妻子“双栖之所”，窗外疏梅筛月影——说的就是三坊七巷里的这座宅院。他三天后牺牲。后来林家卖了房子，冰心的祖父买下，冰心童年也在这里住过
note_en: On the eve of the Guangzhou Uprising of 1911, twenty-four-year-old Lin Juemin wrote his 'Letter to My Wife', remembering the room off the little hall in their house on the back street, with plum blossoms sifting the moonlight outside the window; this is that house, in Fuzhou's Three Lanes and Seven Alleys. He was killed three days later. The family later sold the house to the grandfather of the writer Bing Xin, who spent part of her childhood here
coord_checked: File:林觉民故居 - panoramio.jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:林觉民故居_-_panoramio.jpg

name: Pavilion of Prince Teng, Nanchang
note: 唐代少年才子王勃路过洪州，赴宴时当场写下《滕王阁序》，“落霞与孤鹜齐飞，秋水共长天一色”从此让这座赣江边的楼阁名满天下，与黄鹤楼、岳阳楼并称江南三大名楼。楼阁历代毁了又建，今天的阁楼是 1989 年重建的，登楼仍能望见赣江
note_en: Passing through Hongzhou, the young poet Wang Bo wrote his 'Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng' on the spot at a banquet here, and its line 'the sunset clouds fly with a lone wild duck; the autumn water shares one colour with the endless sky' made this tower on the Gan River famous, one of the three great towers south of the Yangtze. Destroyed and rebuilt many times, the present tower dates from 1989, and from the top you still look out over the river
coord_checked: File:滕王阁 (45128812044).jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:滕王阁_(45128812044).jpg

name: Xiufeng, Mount Lu
note: 李白的《望庐山瀑布》“飞流直下三千尺，疑是银河落九天”写的是香炉峰的瀑布，一般认为就在庐山南麓的秀峰一带，今天叫黄岩瀑布。庐山北面是避暑别墅，南麓秀峰则满是历代文人的摩崖石刻，从景区沿溪上行就能看到瀑布
note_en: Li Bai's 'Viewing the Waterfall at Mount Lu', with its torrent 'plunging three thousand feet, as if the Milky Way were falling from the ninth heaven', describes the falls below Incense Burner Peak, generally placed at Xiufeng on the southern slopes, where they are now called the Huangyan Falls. The north side of the mountain is a hill station of old villas; the south, around Xiufeng, is covered with poems carved into the cliffs, and a path up the stream leads to the falls
coord_checked: File:Lushan Xiufeng Moya 2018.06.10 11-19-11.jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Lushan_Xiufeng_Moya_2018.06.10_11-19-11.jpg

name: Daming Lake, Jinan
note: 刘鹗的《老残游记》写济南“家家泉水，户户垂杨”，老残在大明湖上划船，看见千佛山的倒影映在湖里，比山本身还好看，铁公祠门口一副“四面荷花三面柳，一城山色半城湖”的对联，从此成了济南的名片。这副对联今天仍挂在湖边的铁公祠
note_en: In Liu E's The Travels of Lao Can, Jinan is a city where 'every house has a spring and every door a weeping willow'. Lao Can rows out on Daming Lake and sees the reflection of Thousand Buddha Mountain in the water, finer than the mountain itself, and a couplet at the Shrine of Lord Tie, 'lotus on four sides, willows on three; half the city hills, half the city lake', has stood for Jinan ever since. The couplet still hangs at the shrine by the lake

name: Pu Songling's former residence, Zibo
note: 《聊斋志异》的作者蒲松龄一生科举不第，在淄川蒲家庄的老家和附近的塾馆里教书写作。相传他在村口柳泉边摆茶摊，请过路人讲奇闻怪事，回去写成狐仙鬼怪的故事，所以自号“柳泉居士”。故居里有他的书房“聊斋”，村东柳泉和他的墓都还在
note_en: Pu Songling, author of Strange Tales from a Chinese Studio, failed the imperial examinations all his life and taught and wrote here in his family home at Pujiazhuang and in schools nearby. Legend says he set up a tea stall by the Willow Spring at the edge of the village and gave travellers tea in exchange for strange tales, which he turned into his stories of fox spirits and ghosts. His study, the 'Liaozhai' of the title, the Willow Spring and his grave can all still be seen
coord_checked: Former residence of Pu Songling (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Former_residence_of_Pu_Songling

name: Mount Tai
note: 杜甫年轻时在泰山脚下写下《望岳》，结尾“会当凌绝顶，一览众山小”成了中国人登高最常引用的一句诗。泰山是五岳之首，古代帝王在这里封禅祭天，孔子“登泰山而小天下”。从岱庙到玉皇顶有六千多级石阶，很多人半夜出发爬到日观峰看日出
note_en: Du Fu wrote 'Gazing at Mount Tai' as a young man at the foot of the mountain, ending 'One day I will stand on its very summit and see all other mountains small', the line every Chinese climber quotes. First of the Five Sacred Mountains, Mount Tai is where emperors made sacrifices to heaven, and where Confucius 'climbed and found the world small'. Some six thousand stone steps lead from the Dai Temple to the summit, and many people climb through the night to watch the sunrise from Sun-Viewing Peak

name: Daxiangguo Temple, Kaifeng
note: 《水浒传》里，花和尚鲁智深被派到东京大相国寺看守菜园，一帮泼皮想把他推进粪坑，反被他一脚一个踢下去，他又当众把一棵垂杨柳连根拔起，“倒拔垂杨柳”从此家喻户晓。大相国寺是北宋京城最大的寺院，今天寺里有一尊千手千眼观音，院里还塑着鲁智深拔柳的像
note_en: In Water Margin the fighting monk Lu Zhishen is sent to guard the vegetable garden of the great Xiangguo Temple in the capital; when the local toughs try to tip him into the cesspit he kicks them in one by one, and then pulls a willow tree up by its roots in front of them, one of the best-known scenes in Chinese fiction. Daxiangguo was the greatest temple of the Song capital, and today you can see its thousand-armed Guanyin and a statue of Lu Zhishen uprooting the willow

name: Shaolin Monastery, Mount Song
note: 金庸的武侠小说里，少林寺是天下武学的源头，《天龙八部》最后的大戏就在少室山上：萧峰在群雄面前为父母讨个说法，藏经阁里一位不起眼的扫地老僧化解了几代人的恩怨。少林寺在嵩山少室山下，千佛殿的砖地上留着历代武僧练功踩出的坑，寺西是历代高僧的塔林
note_en: In Jin Yong's martial arts novels the Shaolin Monastery is the fountainhead of all kung fu, and the climax of Demi-Gods and Semi-Devils plays out on its mountain: Xiao Feng confronts the assembled heroes over the truth about his parents, and an unassuming old monk who sweeps the scripture library ends a feud that has run for generations. The monastery stands below Mount Song; inside, the floor of the Thousand Buddha Hall is still pitted by centuries of practice, and the Pagoda Forest of its abbots lies just to the west

name: Yellow Crane Tower, Wuhan
note: 崔颢的《黄鹤楼》“昔人已乘黄鹤去，此地空余黄鹤楼”被宋人推为唐人七律第一，传说李白登楼想题诗，看到崔颢这首便搁笔说“眼前有景道不得”。楼在长江边的蛇山上，历代屡毁屡建，今天的楼是 1985 年重建的，登顶能看到长江大桥和对岸的汉阳
note_en: Cui Hao's 'Yellow Crane Tower', which begins 'The immortal of old has flown off on his yellow crane, and here nothing is left but the Yellow Crane Tower', was judged by Song critics the finest regulated verse of the Tang; legend says Li Bai climbed the tower meaning to write a poem, read Cui Hao's and put down his brush. The tower stands on Snake Hill above the Yangtze; destroyed and rebuilt many times, the present one dates from 1985, and from the top you look over the great river bridge to Hanyang

name: Dongpo Red Cliff, Huanggang
note: 苏轼因“乌台诗案”贬到黄州，1082 年两次在城外江边的赤壁下泛舟夜游，写下前后《赤壁赋》和《念奴娇·赤壁怀古》。其实三国赤壁之战不在这里，苏轼也心知肚明，后人便把这里叫作“东坡赤壁”，以别于真正的古战场。今天岩下的江水已退，赤壁上有二赋堂和东坡的碑刻
note_en: Banished to Huangzhou after a political trial, Su Shi twice boated at night below the red cliffs outside town in 1082 and wrote his two 'Odes on the Red Cliff' and his song lyric on the Red Cliff. The great battle of the Three Kingdoms was not fought here, as Su Shi well knew, so the place is called Dongpo's Red Cliff to tell it from the real battlefield. The river has since drawn back from the rock, which now holds a hall for the two odes and steles of his calligraphy

name: Yueyang Tower
note: 范仲淹没到过岳阳楼，只凭朋友寄来的一幅图写了《岳阳楼记》，“先天下之忧而忧，后天下之乐而乐”成了中国读书人的座右铭。楼在洞庭湖边的岳阳古城西门上，是江南三大名楼中唯一保持古建原貌的一座，今天的主楼是清代重修的，登楼远望就是“衔远山，吞长江”的洞庭湖
note_en: Fan Zhongyan never saw Yueyang Tower; he wrote 'On Yueyang Tower' from a picture a friend sent him, and its maxim 'be first to worry for the world's troubles and last to enjoy its happiness' became the creed of Chinese scholars. The tower stands over the west gate of old Yueyang on the shore of Dongting Lake and is the only one of the three great towers south of the Yangtze still in its old form, rebuilt in the Qing; from the top the lake spreads out just as he imagined it

name: Fenghuang Ancient Town (Shen Congwen's home town)
note: 沈从文 1902 年生在湘西凤凰古城，他的《边城》写湘渝黔三省交界、清水江边的茶峒小镇，渡船、吊脚楼和翠翠的故事，写的正是这片山水。凤凰沿沱江的吊脚楼至今还在，城里有沈从文故居，他的墓在城东听涛山上
note_en: Shen Congwen was born in 1902 in Fenghuang, in the hills of western Hunan, and his novella Border Town, with its ferry, stilt houses and the girl Cuicui, is set in Chadong, a river town on the border where Hunan, Chongqing and Guizhou meet, in the same hill country. Fenghuang's stilt houses still line the Tuo River; his family house is in the old town, and his grave lies on Tingtao Hill to the east

name: Temple of Han Yu, Chaozhou
note: 819 年韩愈因谏迎佛骨被贬到潮州，在任只有八个月，却兴学校、修水利，还写了一篇《祭鳄鱼文》，限江里伤人的鳄鱼七天内迁走，传说鳄鱼真的走了，潮州人把江改名韩江、山改名韩山。韩文公祠是现存最早纪念韩愈的祠堂，就在韩江东岸的韩山上
note_en: In 819 Han Yu was banished to Chaozhou for protesting against the cult of a relic of the Buddha. He governed there for only eight months, but opened schools, built waterworks and wrote his 'Address to the Crocodiles', ordering the man-eating crocodiles in the river to leave within seven days; legend says they did, and the people renamed the river and the hill after him. His temple, the oldest built to him, stands on Han Hill on the east bank of the Han River

name: Liuhou Park, Liuzhou
name_zh: 柳州 · 柳侯公园（柳侯祠）
note: 柳宗元晚年贬为柳州刺史，在这里释放奴婢、开井植树，四年后死在任上。初到柳州，他登上城楼，写下“城上高楼接大荒，海天愁思正茫茫”，寄给同样被贬到南方四州的老友。柳州人为他建了柳侯祠，今天在柳侯公园里，园中有他的衣冠墓和罗池
note_en: Late in life Liu Zongyuan was demoted to governor of Liuzhou, where he freed bondservants, dug wells and planted trees, and died in office four years later. Soon after arriving he climbed the city tower and wrote 'The high tower on the wall looks out on the wilderness; my sorrow is as boundless as sea and sky', sending it to old friends exiled to four other southern towns. The people of Liuzhou built a shrine to him, which now stands in Liuhou Park beside the Luochi pond and his memorial tomb

name: Dongpo Academy, Danzhou
note: 1097 年，六十二岁的苏轼被贬到当时被视为天涯海角的儋州，在这里住了三年，和黎族乡亲往来，办学讲学，海南从此出了第一个举人。他后来说自己一生功业在“黄州惠州儋州”。东坡书院就建在他当年讲学的载酒堂旧址，院里有他和儿子苏过的塑像
note_en: In 1097 Su Shi, aged sixty-two, was banished to Danzhou, then thought of as the very end of the earth. He spent three years here, befriended his Li neighbours and taught, and Hainan soon produced its first successful examination candidate. Looking back, he said the achievements of his life were Huangzhou, Huizhou and Danzhou. Dongpo Academy stands on the site of the hall where he taught, with statues of him and his son

name: Baidicheng (White Emperor City), Fengjie
note: 759 年，流放夜郎途中的李白在白帝城遇赦，立刻乘船东下，写下“朝辞白帝彩云间，千里江陵一日还。两岸猿声啼不住，轻舟已过万重山”。白帝城在瞿塘峡口，刘备在这里托孤给诸葛亮。三峡蓄水后它成了江中小岛，站在岛上能看到印在十元人民币背面的夔门
note_en: In 759 Li Bai, on his way into exile, was pardoned at White Emperor City and set off at once downriver, writing 'At dawn I left Baidi among the rainbow clouds; a thousand li to Jiangling, back in a single day'. Baidicheng guards the mouth of the Qutang Gorge, and it is where Liu Bei entrusted his son to Zhuge Liang. Since the Three Gorges Dam raised the river it has become an island, looking down the gorge to the Kui Gate pictured on the ten-yuan note

name: Wuhou Shrine, Chengdu
note: 杜甫流寓成都时去拜谒诸葛亮的祠堂，写下《蜀相》：“丞相祠堂何处寻？锦官城外柏森森”，结尾“出师未捷身先死，长使英雄泪满襟”让无数读者落泪。武侯祠和刘备的惠陵合在一起，是三国遗迹里最有名的一处，院里的古柏、红墙夹道都还在
note_en: Living in Chengdu as a refugee, Du Fu visited the shrine of Zhuge Liang and wrote 'The Prime Minister of Shu': 'Where shall I find the Prime Minister's shrine? Beyond the walls of the Brocade City, among the dense cypresses', ending with the general who 'died before his campaign was won, and ever since heroes have wept into their sleeves'. Combined with Liu Bei's tomb, the Wuhou Shrine is the most famous site of the Three Kingdoms, still shaded by old cypresses and lined with red walls
coord_checked: Temple of Marquis Wu, Chengdu (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Temple_of_Marquis_Wu,_Chengdu

name: Huangguoshu Waterfall
note: 1638 年徐霞客走到贵州白水河边，先听见雷鸣般的水声，转过山坳看见一溪“悬捣，万练飞空”，水从莲叶般的岩石上漫顶而下，“捣珠崩玉”，他说自己见过的瀑布比它高的有，但从没见过这样宽阔浩大的。这就是今天的黄果树瀑布，水帘后面还有一条可以穿行的水帘洞
note_en: In 1638 Xu Xiake came down to the White Water River in Guizhou, heard a roar like thunder, and rounded a ridge to see a river 'hurled down, ten thousand bolts of silk flying through the air', pouring over a lip of rock like a lotus leaf 'in a crash of pearls and jade'. He had seen taller falls, he wrote, but never one so broad and mighty. This is the Huangguoshu Waterfall, and a passage runs behind the curtain of water

name: Three Pagodas of Chongsheng Temple, Dali
note: 金庸《天龙八部》的主角段誉是大理国王子，书里大理段氏皇族世代出家的天龙寺，就是这座崇圣寺，寺里高僧守着段家的绝学“六脉神剑”，吐蕃国师鸠摩智上门强索，引出一场大战。崇圣寺三塔是大理的标志，背靠苍山，前临洱海，主塔建于唐代
note_en: Duan Yu, hero of Jin Yong's Demi-Gods and Semi-Devils, is a prince of the Kingdom of Dali, and the Tianlong Temple where generations of Duan kings retire as monks is this Chongsheng Temple. Its monks guard the family's secret Six Meridians Divine Sword, and the Tibetan monk Jiumozhi's attempt to seize it leads to a famous battle. The three pagodas, the tallest built in the Tang, are the emblem of Dali, with the Cang Mountains behind and Erhai Lake in front
coord_checked: Three Pagodas of Chongsheng Temple (Dali) (Wikimedia Commons) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Three_Pagodas_of_Chongsheng_Temple_(Dali)

name: Potala Palace, Lhasa
note: 第六世达赖喇嘛仓央嘉措 17 世纪末坐床于布达拉宫，留下几十首情歌，在藏地传唱了三百年，1930 年译成汉文后在内地也广为流传。民间传说他夜里溜出宫，到八廓街的小酒馆会情人。布达拉宫依红山而建，白宫红宫层层叠叠，是拉萨最醒目的建筑
note_en: Tsangyang Gyatso, the Sixth Dalai Lama, was enthroned in the Potala at the end of the seventeenth century and left a few dozen love songs that have been sung across Tibet for three hundred years and were widely read in Chinese after their translation in 1930. Legend has him slipping out of the palace at night to meet a lover in a tavern on the Barkhor. The Potala climbs the Red Hill in tiers of white and red, the landmark of Lhasa

name: Huaqing Palace, Lintong
note: 白居易的《长恨歌》写唐玄宗和杨贵妃的爱情悲剧，“春寒赐浴华清池，温泉水滑洗凝脂”写的就是骊山脚下这座温泉宫，玄宗几乎每年冬天带贵妃来这里住。今天华清宫里有复原的贵妃池、长生殿，夏夜还在骊山下演出大型实景剧《长恨歌》
note_en: Bai Juyi's 'Song of Everlasting Sorrow' tells the tragic love of Emperor Xuanzong and Yang Guifei, and its lines on the spring chill and the warm, smooth water of the Huaqing pools are set in this hot-spring palace at the foot of Mount Li, where the emperor brought her almost every winter. You can see the restored imperial baths and the Hall of Longevity, and on summer nights an open-air show of the poem is staged against the mountain

name: Mount Hua
note: 金庸《射雕英雄传》里，天下五大高手东邪、西毒、南帝、北丐、中神通在华山之巅论剑，争夺“天下第一”的名号，第二次华山论剑也在小说结尾。“华山论剑”从此成了比试高低的代名词。华山是五岳中最险的一座，长空栈道和千尺幢都要贴着绝壁走
note_en: In Jin Yong's The Legend of the Condor Heroes the five greatest masters of the martial world, East Heretic, West Venom, South Emperor, North Beggar and the Central Divine, meet on the summit of Mount Hua to decide who is the best under heaven, and a second contest closes the novel; 'swordplay on Mount Hua' has meant a showdown ever since. Hua is the most precipitous of the Five Sacred Mountains, and its plank walk and Thousand-Foot Precipice cling to sheer rock

name: Yumen Pass
note: 王之涣的《凉州词》“黄河远上白云间，一片孤城万仞山。羌笛何须怨杨柳，春风不度玉门关”写尽了唐代边塞的苍凉，玉门关也成了“出塞”的代名词。汉代这里是丝绸之路通往西域的关口，今天敦煌西北的戈壁上还留着一座方方正正的黄土城堡“小方盘城”和汉长城遗址
note_en: Wang Zhihuan's 'Liangzhou Song', with its lone fort among towering mountains and its line 'the spring wind never crosses the Jade Gate', sums up the desolation of the Tang frontier, and Yumen Pass became shorthand for leaving China behind. In the Han it was the gate of the Silk Road into the Western Regions, and in the gobi northwest of Dunhuang a square fort of rammed earth and stretches of the Han Great Wall still stand

name: Qinghai Lake
note: 唐代诗人笔下的“青海”就是这片中国最大的咸水湖，那时是唐与吐蕃反复争夺的战场。杜甫的《兵车行》写征夫被迫离家，结尾“君不见青海头，古来白骨无人收”，是反战诗里最沉痛的句子。今天湖边是草原和油菜花田，环湖骑行是热门路线，鸟岛上每年夏天有成群的候鸟
note_en: The 'Kokonor' of Tang poetry is this, China's largest saltwater lake, then a battlefield fought over again and again by the Tang and the Tibetan empire. Du Fu's 'Ballad of the Army Carts', on men forced from their homes to fight, ends with the bones by its shore that 'no one has ever gathered', one of the most bitter lines in Chinese poetry. Today the lake is ringed by grassland and rapeseed fields, a favourite route for cyclists, and its Bird Island fills with migrants each summer

name: Zhenbeibu Western Film Studio, Yinchuan
name_zh: 银川 · 镇北堡西部影城
note: 作家张贤亮 20 世纪 60 年代在宁夏劳改时见到这两座明清边堡的废墟，把它写进小说《绿化树》。1993 年他用稿费把废墟改成影视城，《红高粱》《大话西游》《新龙门客栈》都在这里拍过外景，他自己说是“出卖荒凉”。今天古堡里保留着这些电影的布景
note_en: The writer Zhang Xianliang came across the ruins of these two Ming and Qing frontier forts while in a labour camp in Ningxia in the 1960s and put them into his novel Mimosa. In 1993 he used his royalties to turn the ruins into a film studio, 'selling desolation', as he put it, and Red Sorghum, A Chinese Odyssey and New Dragon Gate Inn were all shot here. The sets from those films are still in the old forts
coord_checked: File:镇北堡西部影城.jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:镇北堡西部影城.jpg

name: Altay
note: 李娟的《我的阿勒泰》写她在阿勒泰地区跟着母亲开小卖部、做裁缝的日子：哈萨克牧民转场、雪原上的冬窝子、喀吾图的小村子，平淡又有趣。2024 年改编成电视剧后，阿勒泰成了热门旅行地。阿勒泰市在阿尔泰山南麓，夏天往北是草原和喀纳斯湖，冬天是中国最好的滑雪场之一
note_en: Li Juan's My Altay is about the years she spent in the Altay region with her mother, who ran a small shop and did tailoring for the Kazakh herders: the moves to the summer pastures, winter camps in the snow, the little village of Kawutu, all told plainly and with a lot of humour. Since the 2024 TV adaptation Altay has become a popular place to visit. The town sits at the foot of the Altai Mountains, with grassland and Kanas Lake to the north in summer and some of China's best skiing in winter

name: Chihkan Tower (Fort Provintia), Tainan
note: 台南人连横用十年写成《台湾通史》，序言开头一句“台湾固无史也，荷人启之，郑氏作之，清代营之”，概括了这座岛三百年的历史。赤崁楼正是这段历史的见证：荷兰人 1653 年在这里建普罗民遮城，郑成功收复台湾后改作承天府。今天的楼阁是清代在荷兰城堡的残基上建的
note_en: Lian Heng of Tainan spent ten years writing The General History of Taiwan, whose preface opens 'Taiwan had no history: the Dutch began it, the Zheng family built it, the Qing developed it', three centuries of the island in a sentence. Chihkan Tower is witness to all of it: the Dutch built Fort Provintia here in 1653, and after Koxinga took the island it became the seat of his government. The present pavilions were built in the Qing on the brick foundations of the Dutch fort

name: The Repulse Bay (site of the Repulse Bay Hotel), Hong Kong
name_zh: 香港 · 浅水湾（浅水湾酒店旧址）
note: 张爱玲的《倾城之恋》里，上海离婚女子白流苏随范柳原来到香港，住进浅水湾饭店，两人在海滩、在那堵灰砖墙下互相试探；直到日军进攻香港，一座城的沦陷成全了两个人。浅水湾饭店 1982 年拆除，原址建了公寓楼“影湾园”，复刻了当年饭店的露台餐厅，楼下就是浅水湾海滩
note_en: In Eileen Chang's Love in a Fallen City, Bai Liusu, a divorcee from Shanghai, follows Fan Liuyuan to Hong Kong and takes a room at the Repulse Bay Hotel, where the two circle each other on the beach and beneath a grey brick wall, until the Japanese attack on Hong Kong and the fall of a whole city bring them together. The hotel was demolished in 1982 and replaced by the apartment block called The Repulse Bay, which recreates the hotel's old Verandah restaurant, above the beach

name: A-Ma Temple, Macau
note: 相传葡萄牙人初到澳门，在这座妈祖庙前登岸，问地名，当地人答“妈阁”，“Macau”由此得名。闻一多 1925 年写《七子之歌》，第一首就是《澳门》：“你可知‘妈港’不是我的真名姓”，1999 年澳门回归时谱曲传唱。妈阁庙是澳门最古老的庙宇，今天香火仍旺
note_en: The story goes that when the Portuguese first landed here and asked the name of the place, they were told 'Ma Kok', after this temple to the sea goddess Mazu, and so the city became Macau. In 1925 Wen Yiduo wrote 'Song of the Seven Sons', and its first song is Macau's: 'Do you know that Macau is not my real name?' Set to music, it was sung everywhere at the handover in 1999. The temple, the oldest in Macau, climbs the hillside and is still busy with worshippers

name: Temple of Earth (Ditan Park), Beijing
note: 史铁生二十一岁双腿瘫痪，此后十五年，他几乎天天摇着轮椅进家附近荒芜的地坛，在古柏下想生与死，想母亲，写成了散文《我与地坛》。地坛是明清皇帝祭地的地方，今天是公园，方泽坛和古柏林都在，春节有庙会，秋天有书市
note_en: Paralysed in both legs at twenty-one, Shi Tiesheng wheeled himself almost every day for fifteen years into the overgrown Temple of Earth near his home, and under its old cypresses thought about life and death and about his mother, the subject of his essay The Temple of Earth and I. The altar where Ming and Qing emperors made offerings to the earth is now a park, with the square altar and the cypress groves still there, a temple fair at Spring Festival and a book fair in autumn

name: Shanghai's longtang lanes (Tianzifang)
name_zh: 上海 · 石库门弄堂（田子坊）
note: 王安忆的《长恨歌》开篇整整一章写上海的弄堂，主人公王琦瑶是“弄堂里的女儿”，四十年的悲欢都没离开过弄堂。泰康路的田子坊是今天最容易走进的一片石库门老弄堂，房子里开着小店和咖啡馆，楼上仍有人家住着
note_en: Wang Anyi's The Song of Everlasting Sorrow opens with a whole chapter on the lanes of Shanghai, and its heroine Wang Qiyao is a daughter of the longtang who never leaves them in forty years of love and loss. Tianzifang, off Taikang Road, is the easiest of the old shikumen lane neighbourhoods to wander into today, its houses now full of small shops and cafés, with families still living upstairs

name: Former Ginling Women's College (Nanjing Normal University)
name_zh: 南京 · 金陵女子大学旧址（南京师范大学随园校区）
prototype_of: 严歌苓的《金陵十三钗》写 1937 年南京沦陷时，躲进一座美国教堂的女学生和十三个秦淮河妓女的故事。她说灵感来自金陵女子文理学院教务长魏特琳的日记，魏特琳当年在这座校园里收容了上万名妇女和儿童。校园今天是南京师范大学随园校区，大屋顶的老建筑都还在
prototype_of_en: Yan Geling's The Flowers of War tells of schoolgirls and thirteen courtesans from the Qinhuai River hiding in an American church when Nanjing fell in 1937. She has said the story grew out of the diary of Minnie Vautrin, dean of Ginling Women's College, who sheltered some ten thousand women and children on this campus. It is now the Suiyuan campus of Nanjing Normal University, and its old buildings with their great Chinese-style roofs are all still standing
coord_checked: File:南师大教育馆3.jpg (Wikimedia Commons, photo location) — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:南师大教育馆3.jpg

name: Longchuan, Dehong (Yunnan)
note: 1969 年，十七岁的王小波从北京来到中缅边境的陇川插队，在这里过了两年知青生活。后来他写《黄金时代》，让二十一岁的知青王二在云南山里的农场和队医陈清扬相恋，用的就是这段日子的底子。陇川今天是德宏的边境县城，景颇族的目瑙纵歌节最有名
note_en: Wang Xiaobo was seventeen when he was sent from Beijing to Longchuan, on the Burmese border, as an educated youth in 1969, and spent two years here. His novel The Golden Age, about the twenty-one-year-old sent-down youth Wang Er and the farm doctor Chen Qingyang in the hills of Yunnan, draws on those years. Longchuan is now a border county town in Dehong, best known for the Jingpo people's Munao Zongge festival

name: 228 Peace Memorial Park (the New Park), Taipei
name_zh: 台北 · 二二八和平纪念公园（新公园）
note: 白先勇的《孽子》写七十年代被家里赶出来的同性恋少年，夜里聚在台北新公园的莲花池边，把这里叫作“我们的王国”，这本书是台湾同志文学的经典。新公园 1996 年改名二二八和平纪念公园，莲花池、凉亭和台湾博物馆都还在
note_en: Pai Hsien-yung's Crystal Boys follows gay teenagers in 1970s Taipei, thrown out by their families, who gather at night around the lotus pond in the New Park and call it their kingdom; it is a classic of Taiwanese gay literature. The New Park was renamed 228 Peace Memorial Park in 1996, and the pond, the pavilions and the National Taiwan Museum are all still there

name: Lin Haiyin's former residence (Jinjiang Guild Hall), Beijing
note: 林海音的《城南旧事》借小英子的眼睛写她童年时的北京城南：胡同、骆驼队、惠安馆里的“疯子”。她小时候随家人在南柳巷这座晋江会馆住了八年，故居修缮后 2025 年免费开放，院里有一间叫“冬青书屋”的阅览室
note_en: Lin Haiyin's My Memories of Old Beijing is her childhood in the south of the city seen through the eyes of little Yingzi: the hutongs, the camel trains, the 'madwoman' of the Hui'an Guild Hall. As a girl she lived for eight years with her family in this guild hall on Nanliu Lane; restored, it opened free to the public in 2025, with a reading room called the Dongqing Study

name: National Chengchi University, Taipei
note: 林奕含以高分考上医学系，读了两周就退学，重考进政大中文系。她唯一的小说《房思琪的初恋乐园》写补习班名师诱骗一个十三岁的女孩，追问文学怎么会被拿来粉饰伤害，2017 年出版，同年她去世。政大校园在台北木栅指南山下，依山而建
note_en: Lin Yi-han won a place at medical school with top marks, left after two weeks, and sat the exams again to study Chinese literature here. Her only novel, Fang Si-Chi's First Love Paradise, about a celebrated cram-school teacher who grooms a thirteen-year-old girl, asks how literature can be used to dress up harm; it came out in 2017, the year she died. The campus climbs the foot of Zhinan Mountain in Muzha, Taipei

name: Chadong (Biancheng town), Hunan
note: 沈从文的《边城》就发生在这里：湘西边境的小山城茶峒，溪边白塔下住着摆渡的老人和孙女翠翠。茶峒 2005 年改名边城镇，在湘渝黔三省交界的清水江边，拉绳摆渡的拉拉渡还在渡人，对岸就是重庆洪安，有“一脚跨三省”的界碑
note_en: Shen Congwen set Border Town here, in Chadong, a small hill town on the western edge of Hunan, where an old ferryman and his granddaughter Cuicui live below a white pagoda by the stream. Renamed Biancheng in 2005, it sits on the Qingshui River where Hunan, Chongqing and Guizhou meet; the Lala Ferry still hauls passengers across on a rope to Hong'an in Chongqing, and a stone marks the spot where you can stand in three provinces at once
